newcomerCriteria:
Home language survey at enrolment
A Language Proficiency Assessment Committee decides identification and placement

Texas Education Code §§ 29.051–29.064 and 19 TAC Ch. 89, Subch. BB
removalCriteria:
TELPAS Advanced High in all four domains
Plus a qualifying score on a standardised reading assessment — STAAR Reading or English I/II
Plus a teacher evaluation on a state-standardised rubric
From 2026/27 the parental-approval requirement becomes notice only

newcomerProportion.note: emergent bilingual students, up from 18.8% in 2017-18; ~10% identified as newcomers, 13% dually identified with disabilities

l2Support:
Two statutory models — Bilingual Education, including dual-language, and ESL
Funded through a weighted bilingual/ESL allotment under the Foundation School Program
Ten standardised parent-communication letters are mandated statewide at each step
l1Support:
Bilingual education — native-language instruction transitioning to English
A required option once a language group reaches about 20 pupils in a grade at a campus
Texas Education Code § 29.053

newcomerCriteria:
Home-language screening survey, then the WIDA Screener
Determines multilingual-learner eligibility
RCW Chapter 28A.180 — Transitional Bilingual Instruction Act 1979
removalCriteria:
Annual WIDA ACCESS — composite 4.0 in grades K–1, 4.7 in grades 2–12
From the 2024 cycle, grades 3–12 may also exit on 4.3–4.6 with level 3/4 on state ELA
Two years' post-exit monitoring is mandatory

newcomerProportion.note: served via TBIP; statewide % of total enrollment not confirmed from a single clean source

l2Support:
The Transitional Bilingual Instruction Program is the statewide frame
State funding flows through a per-pupil TBIP formula
Since 2019–20, teachers delivering TBIP must hold a bilingual or ELL endorsement
l1Support:
The Transitional Bilingual Instruction Program is native-language transitional by design
OSPI also promotes Dual Language programmes statewide alongside it

policyHistory.description: Senate Bill 2149 establishes the Transitional Bilingual Instruction Act (RCW 28A.180).
New teacher bilingual/ELL endorsement requirement takes effect for TBIP-funded instructors.
Expanded WIDA exit pathway added (4.3-4.6 + ELA Level 3/4) for grades 3-12.
